Sylvia De La Fuentes
Fresno, CA 93723 | The1stroundpick@gmail.com | 559-721-3608
 

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Team,
When I think about Support and the importance of support while someone fights to transform their life in addiction and mental health care, I know firsthand that when someone reaches out for support, that first human connection can change everything. I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. At Aetna as a Medicare Customer Service Representative, I handled high-volume inbound calls and outbound follow-ups, verified eligibility details, and maintained strict HIPAA compliance while supporting members through complex coverage questions. Additionally, my experience managing Salesforce CRM datasets and high-volume workflows at Oriental Motor taught me how to move quickly across multiple live queues, stay organized in a technology-enabled environment, and treat metrics as tools to improve service quality rather than sources of pressure.

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID.

Celena Ditz, MS, LMFT
Kings Mountain, NC
(704) 418-2440 | celditz@gmail.com

October 26, 2026

Hiring Committee
Launch AWA NC
Re: Clinic Director – Adolescent Mental Health

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Clinic Director – Adolescent Mental Health position with Launch AWA NC. As a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist with more than 25 years of experience in clinical and child-and-family services, including over 15 years in program and clinical leadership, I bring a combination of clinical expertise, operational management, staff development, and a strong commitment to improving outcomes for children, adolescents, and families. I am excited about the opportunity to apply my experience to a role focused on adolescent mental health and the delivery of high-quality, accessible clinical services.

In my current role as Director of Programs at Children’s Homes of Cleveland County/Core Family Services, I provide senior clinical and operational leadership across outpatient therapy, residential, independent living, and adoption programs. I also serve as Clinical Director of outpatient therapy, where I oversee clinical quality, clinician recruitment and supervision, service capacity, reimbursement, compliance, and ongoing program development. Throughout my tenure, I have worked to strengthen clinical services, support staff effectiveness, and ensure that programs meet the needs of the individuals and families they serve while maintaining appropriate clinical, contractual, and regulatory standards.

My experience has provided me with a strong understanding of the balance required to lead a successful behavioral health clinic. I have experience developing clinical capacity in response to community needs, supporting clinicians through supervision and consultation, managing after-hours clinical coverage for therapeutic emergencies, and collaborating with executive leadership on staffing, budgeting, and organizational planning. I believe effective clinical leadership requires both a commitment to sound clinical practice and the ability to build the systems, relationships, and processes that allow clinicians to provide meaningful, consistent care.

I also bring extensive experience in trauma-informed care, quality improvement, and clinical standards. As a Statewide Clinical Coach with Benchmarks NC Partnering for Excellence, I train, review, and evaluate trauma-intensive clinical assessments completed by clinicians across North Carolina, providing feedback and supporting consistency with established clinical standards. Additionally, I coordinate my agency’s performance and quality improvement and accreditation activities, including staff training, record reviews, corrective action planning, and continuous improvement initiatives. These experiences have strengthened my ability to evaluate clinical practices, identify opportunities for improvement, support professional development, and promote accountability while maintaining a focus on quality care.

In addition to my clinical background, I hold a Master of Science in Marriage and Family Therapy and a Master of Business Administration. This combination allows me to approach clinical leadership with an understanding of both the therapeutic needs of adolescents and families and the operational and financial considerations necessary to sustain and grow effective services. I value collaborative leadership, clear communication, thoughtful decision-making, and creating an environment where clinicians feel supported in their work and equipped to provide the highest quality of care.

Throughout my career, I have remained committed to serving children and families, particularly those impacted by trauma and other significant life challenges. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my experience to Launch AWA NC and help strengthen mental health services for adolescents. Given my extensive experience, clinical background, and leadership responsibilities, I would also welcome a conversation about compensation. I recognize that the position has a posted salary range; however, I am seeking compensation above that range that more fully reflects my qualifications and the value I would bring to the role. I hope there may be flexibility to discuss a package that aligns with my experience and the position’s responsibilities.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, leadership experience, and commitment to serving adolescents and families could contribute to the continued success of Launch AWA NC.

Sincerely,
Celena Ditz, MS, LMFT

Re: Clinic Director: Adolescent Mental Health | Launch AWA North Carolina

Dear Hiring Committee:
I am excited to apply for the Clinic Director position leading the launch of Adolescent Wellness Academy’s first North Carolina clinic. As a licensed clinical social work and case management leader with more than 15 years of experience across behavioral health, healthcare, higher education, and community services, I offer the clinical supervision, operational leadership, and change-management experience needed to build a strong program from the ground up. AWA’s opportunity to create a focused, family-centered PHP/IOP clinic for adolescents is especially compelling to me because it combines direct clinical impact with the chance to shape culture, quality, and sustainable growth from day one.

Throughout my career, I have led complex case coordination, crisis response, care transitions, quality assurance, policy development, talent development, budgeting, and resource allocation. I have also provided clinical supervision and operational management while partnering with healthcare providers, hospital leaders, community agencies, and other stakeholders. These experiences would enable me to recruit and develop clinicians, establish clear clinical and documentation standards, guide level-of-care decisions, and build trusted relationships with families and referral partners across North Carolina.

I would bring a practical, outcomes-focused approach to launch execution: hiring and onboarding a cohesive team; creating a supportive environment for early-career clinicians; establishing reliable crisis, documentation, and quality-review processes; and using assessment findings and utilization trends to strengthen care delivery. My Master of Social Work and ongoing Doctor of Social Work studies in leadership further support my ability to connect evidence-informed clinical practice with disciplined operations and organizational growth.

AWA’s values—Dare to Grow, Contribute to the Whole, Choose Kindness, Spread Optimism, and Deliver Results—reflect how I strive to lead: with accountability, collaboration, compassion, and a clear commitment to excellent outcomes. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical and operational leadership can help AWA launch a high-quality adolescent program and establish a strong foundation for long-term success in North Carolina.
Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Ty Matthews, LCSW, LISW-CP, DSW (C)

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I’m excited to apply for the remote Utilization Review Specialist – Behavioral Health position at Principles Recovery Center. My background combines hands-on behavioral health documentation and review support with outpatient addiction and mental health program leadership, giving me a strong foundation for the role’s authorization and medical-necessity workflows.

In my current role as Behavioral Health Documentation & Review Support at Kings Consulting and Analytics, LLC, I support documentation review for substance use disorder and mental health cases. I review intakes, diagnoses, treatment history, progress notes, service documentation, and supporting clinical records to identify gaps and help ensure records are complete, consistent, and ready for utilization review. I also synthesize clinical details in EHR/KIPU workflows to support authorization-related documentation, level-of-care alignment, and timely review decisions. Working alongside an experienced behavioral health consulting team has strengthened my review accuracy and understanding of utilization review processes.

Previously, as Program Director at Meta Addiction Treatment, I developed substantial experience in outpatient addiction and mental health services, program leadership, and case management. That work strengthened my ability to coordinate across teams, support treatment planning and continuity of care, maintain clear documentation, and keep client needs and program requirements in view.

I’m prepared to bring this experience to benefit and eligibility verification, prior authorization and pre-certification workflows, concurrent and continued-stay reviews, and medical-necessity support. My background includes supporting level-of-care alignment and authorization documentation; I’m ready to build on that foundation with the specific review standards and procedures used by Principles Recovery Center.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my documentation review experience and behavioral health program background can contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Lindsey Duran

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the Admissions Counselor position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With six years of experience in education as a Teacher's Assistant and Guidance Counselor, along with over five years of experience in healthcare, including mental health and substance use services, I bring a diverse professional background and a genuine passion for helping adolescents and families navigate life's challenges.

Throughout my career, I have developed a strong ability to build meaningful connections with individuals from all walks of life. My experience has taught me that effective guidance begins with understanding, compassion, and the ability to meet people where they are without judgment. Whether working with students, patients, or families, I believe every individual deserves to feel respected, heard, and valued. I approach every interaction with the understanding that I am not above the person seeking support; I am there to walk alongside them, offer guidance, and help them recognize their own potential.

My background in mental health and substance use services has further strengthened my ability to communicate with empathy, navigate sensitive situations, and establish trust with individuals experiencing vulnerable moments in their lives. My own personal experiences with loss and adversity have also shaped my perspective, deepening my appreciation for resilience, compassion, and the importance of having someone who genuinely believes in you. These experiences have reinforced my commitment to treating every individual with dignity rather than defining them by their circumstances.

My colleagues would describe me as ambitious, focused, reliable, and grounding. I take pride in my ability to bridge the gap between professionalism and relatability, creating connections that allow people to feel comfortable, supported, and understood. I believe my combined experience in education, healthcare, mental health, and substance use services gives me a unique perspective that aligns with the mission of supporting adolescents and their families through important and sometimes difficult transitions.

I am particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy because I value the opportunity to be part of an organization that prioritizes adolescent wellness, personal growth, and individualized support. I would be honored to bring my professional experience, personal perspective, and genuine dedication to helping others to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, compassion, and commitment to serving others would make me a valuable addition to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Amanda Nieves-Rodriguez

Dear AWA Academy Team,

I am so excited to apply for the opportunity to join AWA Academy’s IOP/PHP team working with adolescents. As a therapist who graduated in December 2025, I am eager to continue growing as a clinician in a setting that aligns with something I am truly passionate about: supporting children, adolescents, and their families. I am especially drawn to AWA Academy because of the impact your work has on the lives of children and families, and I would love to be part of that mission.

I currently work as an intake therapist for a virtual IOP program, where I work with both adults and children. I also have experience working in an inpatient psychiatric hospital with adults, where I facilitated group therapy and conducted intake assessments. These experiences have helped me build my clinical skills, connect with clients from different backgrounds, and better understand the importance of compassionate, individualized care.

Before becoming a therapist, I worked as a special education teacher with children on the autism spectrum. Working with children and families was one of the most meaningful parts of my professional journey and played a big role in shaping the kind of therapist I wanted to become. I genuinely love working with kids and helping them feel understood, supported, and empowered. I would love the opportunity to bring that passion into my clinical work with adolescents and their families.

My therapeutic approach incorporates concepts from ACT and DBT, and I am excited to continue building on these skills while gaining more experience in individual therapy. I am eager to learn, grow, and challenge myself as a clinician, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to do so alongside a team that shares my commitment to supporting young people through difficult moments in their lives.

I am also fluent in both English and Portuguese, which allows me to connect with and support families from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds. I currently hold a license as a Registered Mental Health Intern and have a qualified supervisor. I anticipate to become fully licensed in a year and a half.

I would be genuinely excited to join AWA Academy and contribute to the meaningful work you do with children and families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would love the opportunity to connect and share more about my experience and enthusiasm for this role!

Thank you!

Rebecca Ubertini

October 23, 2026 

Dear Hiring Committee, 

Thank you for taking the time to review my resume and cover letter. I am writing to express my enthusiasm for the opportunity to continue my experience working as a Registered Mental Health Counseling Intern at  Adolescent Wellness Academy. I received a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and am a recent graduate with my Masters in Mental Health Counseling from the University of Miami. 

As a motivated and compassionate clinician, I am interested in expanding my experience of working with evidence-based treatment modalities. 

My educational experiences have helped me to build my knowledge and experience for working as a registered mental health counseling intern. I have a strong academic background in psychology, as well as a strong interest in working with children and their families to address mental health challenges at an early age, including Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, Anxiety, and Depression. Through my recent experiences working as a practicum intern at Nicklaus Children’s Hospital and the Institute for Individual and Family Counseling, I was able to establish a strong foundation in conceptualizing cases, applying interventions and building rapport. 

In my previous experience working at Florida International University’s Summer Treatment Program, I had the opportunity to work directly with children and their families, providing support in areas such as emotional regulation, coping skills, and behavioral management. These experiences have provided a good foundation in implementing therapeutic strategies tailored to the unique needs of young children, as well as solidified my interest in child and adolescent mental health. 

I have a passion for working with programs that help to provide low-cost services for a diverse population, as highlighted in my experience working as a practicum intern at the institute for Individual and Family Counseling. I believe that my strong communication skills and dedication will allow for a wonderful learning experience as I continue my work in the field of mental health counseling.  

I have included my resume and look forward to the possibility of discussing further my qualifications. Please feel welcome to contact me at your earliest convenience. I look forward to hearing from you. 

Respectfully, 
Morgan Reilly

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., NCC

Hiring Committee
Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA)
Boca Raton, Florida


Re: Primary Therapist Position

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) in Boca Raton, Florida. With a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision, a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and experience in clinical practice, counselor education, and clinical training, I bring an integrated perspective on mental health care that combines evidence-informed clinical approaches, developmental knowledge, multicultural awareness, and a commitment to supporting individuals through challenging life transitions. Having recently relocated back to Florida from Connecticut, I am currently working toward full licensure with the State of Florida and practicing as a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI). I am also legally authorized to live and work in the United States without employer sponsorship. I am particularly interested in AWA’s work with adolescents and its emphasis on individualized, collaborative care that supports emotional well-being, resilience, and personal growth, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s work with adolescents and families from diverse backgrounds.

As a Portuguese-English bilingual professional with Spanish skills, I bring a multicultural perspective that supports my commitment to culturally responsive and accessible mental health care. My Brazilian background and international experience have shaped my appreciation for the ways culture, identity, family expectations, and transitions influence individuals’ experiences and help-seeking behaviors. I recognize the importance of building therapeutic relationships that honor clients’ culture and lived experiences while fostering trust, collaboration, and respect. 

My clinical experience and interests include working with concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, substance use/abuse, domestic violence, acculturation, relationship difficulties, and life transitions. My therapeutic approach reflects evidence-informed assimilative integration, grounded primarily in Narrative Therapy and Relational-Cultural Theory (RCT), while incorporating complementary approaches such as Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to meet clients’ unique needs and therapeutic goals. I strive to create a warm, collaborative, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment in which clients can explore their experiences, identify strengths, develop effective coping strategies, and work toward meaningful goals. My approach is grounded in cultural humility, trauma-responsive care, and an understanding of how relationships, family systems, cultural contexts, and broader social factors influence mental health and development.

I have a particular interest in human development across the lifespan, which is reflected in both my clinical work and my teaching. As an instructor, I have taught Lifespan and Human Development to counseling students, a course that deepens my engagement with developmental theories and how biological, psychological, social, cultural, and relational factors shape individuals’ experiences and well-being at different stages of life. This academic focus complements my interest in working with adolescents and understanding the unique developmental, emotional, interpersonal, and family-related challenges they may experience. I value developmentally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approaches that recognize each young person’s needs while engaging families and other members of the treatment team to support growth, resilience, and emotional well-being.

My clinical background also includes experience with individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. In Brazil, I developed a project focused on social inclusion and group counseling for individuals with developmental disabilities, which gave me valuable experience understanding and addressing social, interpersonal, developmental, and emotional needs. This experience strengthened my commitment to adapting support to individuals’ unique circumstances and fostering environments that promote inclusion, connection, and personal growth. My background in career counseling further strengthened my experience supporting young individuals as they navigate transitions, develop self-awareness, and identify meaningful paths forward.

In addition to my clinical work, I served as an Assistant Professor of Practice and Clinical Training Director at Fairfield University in Connecticut, where I taught and mentored counseling students, coordinated clinical placements, collaborated with clinical supervisors and community partners, and supported students’ professional development. My responsibilities included coordinating field placements, communicating with supervisors and training sites, and helping students connect academic knowledge with clinical practice. This experience strengthened my ability to respectfully collaborate across professional roles, communicate effectively, maintain organized documentation, and appreciate the importance of coordinated care and professional accountability. My teaching experience in counseling skills, advanced treatment and counseling interventions, group work, ethics, career counseling, and human development also informs my understanding of therapeutic relationships, treatment planning, and the importance of adapting interventions to clients’ developmental and contextual needs.

I believe I am drawn to AWA’s multidisciplinary treatment environment and the opportunity to collaborate with therapists, psychiatrists, and other clinical professionals to support adolescents’ mental health and well-being. I value comprehensive, individualized treatment that integrates assessment, collaborative goal setting, therapeutic interventions, ongoing progress evaluation, family engagement, and continuity of care. I also recognize the importance of timely, accurate clinical documentation, ethical practice, appropriate consultation, and coordination with the treatment team to promote effective, consistent care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, expertise in counselor education and human development, multicultural perspective, and commitment to accessible, trauma-responsive, strengths-based, and evidence-informed care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families it serves.

Sincerely,

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., M.S., NCC
Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern
+1 (561) 289-5680 | paula@lm2services.com

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With a professional background as a Behavior Analyst, I have developed strong skills in communication, assessment, crisis management, documentation, and working with individuals and families navigating challenging situations. I am eager to bring these skills into a mental health setting where I can help adolescents and their families access the support and treatment they need.

Throughout my experience as a Behavior Analyst, I have worked closely with individuals with diverse behavioral, emotional, and developmental needs. My responsibilities have required me to build rapport, communicate effectively with families and caregivers, gather and evaluate sensitive information, maintain accurate documentation, and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams. I have also developed the ability to remain calm under pressure, navigate emotionally difficult situations, and approach each individual with patience, empathy, and professionalism.

I believe my background has prepared me well for the responsibilities of an admissions role, particularly when working with teenagers and families who may be experiencing uncertainty, stress, or crisis. I understand the importance of making individuals feel heard, respected, and supported during vulnerable moments. I would bring a compassionate, organized, and solution-oriented approach to helping prospective clients navigate the admissions process and connecting them with appropriate mental health services.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to continue making a meaningful difference in the lives of adolescents while expanding my professional experience into the mental health field. I am confident that my interpersonal skills, attention to detail, adaptability, and commitment to helping others would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and transferable skills could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Kayla Kraemer

•	Provide supervision and leadership to staff
•	Interpret reports and monitor data to achieve the agency’s mission

candidates.cover_letter:
April Aragon

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a bachelor's degree in Psychology, continued graduate-level education in professional counseling, and a diverse background in psychiatric care, behavioral health, crisis intervention, residential services, and remote patient engagement, I believe I would be a strong addition to your team.

Throughout my professional experience, I have developed a genuine passion for working within mental health services and helping individuals and families navigate challenging circumstances. My background includes working as a Patient Engagement Specialist with Island Psychiatry, where I gained direct experience within a psychiatric healthcare setting. I have also worked in crisis behavioral health services as a QMHP with Avail Solutions, as well as in residential and youth behavioral health settings. These experiences strengthened my understanding of mental health needs, the importance of compassionate communication, and the role that timely access to appropriate care can play in an individual's well-being.

Additionally, my current experience working within a women's shelter has further developed my ability to support vulnerable populations, maintain professionalism in sensitive situations, and approach individuals from diverse backgrounds with empathy and understanding.

Beyond my healthcare experience, I bring approximately three years of remote telephone-based customer service experience. I worked for one year with Alorica handling inbound calls and approximately two years with US Legal conducting outbound calls. These positions strengthened my ability to communicate effectively over the phone, manage conversations independently, address questions and concerns, and maintain professionalism in a fast-paced remote work environment.

I believe this combination of clinical exposure, behavioral health experience, education, and remote communication skills makes me particularly well-suited for an admissions position. I understand that for many families, reaching out to a mental health facility can be an emotional and sometimes overwhelming first step. I would approach every interaction with patience, compassion, and professionalism while helping families feel informed, supported, and comfortable throughout the admissions process.

I am especially interested in the opportunity to contribute to an organization dedicated to adolescent mental health and wellness. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, dedication, and passion for behavioral healthcare to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and qualifications align with your team's needs.

Sincerely,

April Aragon

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With experience in remote behavioral health intake, client coordination, and crisis intervention, along with my current pursuit of a Master of Social Work at the University of Nevada, Reno, I believe my background aligns well with the needs of your admissions team.

In my previous remote role as an Intake Coordinator at Morning View Family Therapy, I supported individuals seeking mental health services, managed inquiries, coordinated appointments, and helped clients navigate the intake process. Working remotely strengthened my ability to stay organized, manage responsibilities independently, maintain accurate documentation, and communicate effectively without direct supervision. I also understand how important the first interaction can be, particularly when someone is reaching out for help during a difficult or overwhelming time.

More recently, during my clinical practicum at U.S.VETS Las Vegas, I worked directly with veterans experiencing serious mental illness, substance use disorders, and significant life challenges. My responsibilities included conducting biopsychosocial assessments, providing supportive counseling, facilitating therapeutic groups, and responding to individuals experiencing emotional distress or crisis. These experiences strengthened my ability to remain calm under pressure, approach sensitive conversations with compassion, and recognize when individuals need additional support or intervention.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to combine my administrative and clinical experience to help individuals and families access appropriate treatment. I recognize that reaching out for mental health or substance use services can be intimidating, and I would welcome the opportunity to make that process feel less overwhelming. I am comfortable working independently, managing confidential information, and ensuring that individuals receive consistent communication and follow-through.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience in remote behavioral health intake and direct client services could contribute to your admissions team. I look forward to the possibility of supporting the important work being done at both programs.

Sincerely,  
Alison Streicher

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy. As an internationally trained psychologist from Chile with nine years of professional experience in mental health, psychosocial intervention, and community-based work, I believe my academic background, clinical experience, and multicultural perspective would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your organization.

Throughout my professional career, I have worked with children, adolescents, families, and individuals experiencing complex psychosocial circumstances. My experience includes individual psychological support, family intervention, psychosocial assessment, emotional and behavioral difficulties, trauma-informed approaches, crisis intervention, and interdisciplinary collaboration. I have worked in clinical, educational, community, and child protection settings, developing a comprehensive understanding of the emotional, developmental, social, and environmental factors that influence adolescent well-being.

My academic background includes a Master’s degree in Migration, Human Rights and Social Management, as well as postgraduate training in Educational Psychology and Child and Adolescent Psychology. These qualifications have strengthened my understanding of social vulnerability, cultural diversity, human rights, family dynamics, and the importance of providing accessible, inclusive, and culturally responsive mental health support.

One of my strongest professional assets is my multicultural and multilingual background. Born in the United States and raised in Chile, I have developed a strong understanding of different cultural contexts and the challenges associated with migration, identity, cultural adaptation, and belonging. I am bilingual in Spanish and English, with additional knowledge of Portuguese and Catalan. I consider cultural sensitivity, empathy, active listening, adaptability, and respect for individual differences essential competencies when working with adolescents and their families.

I am particularly interested in Adolescent Wellness Academy because of its commitment to adolescent mental health and its family-centered approach. I strongly believe that effective psychological support requires not only an understanding of individual symptoms, but also attention to family relationships, social environments, cultural backgrounds, and each young person’s unique experiences.

In addition to my clinical and psychosocial experience, I bring strong communication, teamwork, problem-solving, organizational, and interpersonal skills. I am comfortable collaborating with multidisciplinary teams, communicating with diverse populations, adapting to different professional environments, and approaching challenging situations with professionalism, compassion, and ethical responsibility.

As an internationally trained psychologist, I understand the distinction between my professional qualifications in Chile and the licensing requirements for independent psychological practice in the United States. I would welcome opportunities aligned with my credentials, experience, and applicable professional requirements.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to discuss how my background, professional competencies, and cross-cultural experience could contribute to your team and the well-being of the adolescents and families you serve.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Hiring Manager

Intake and Engagement Coordinator Position

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Full-Time Intake and Engagement Coordinator position at Seven Starling. I currently work for Oklahoma Human Services and am pursuing my bachelor's degree in Social Work at East Central University. I will be graduating in December 10th, 2026. Through my education and work experience, I have developed strong communication, case management, and organizational skills that I believe would make me a great fit for your team.

In my current position with Oklahoma Human Services, I work directly with families who are facing difficult situations and need guidance, support, and access to services. A large part of my job involves communicating with clients, making phone calls, coordinating with service providers, completing assessments, and maintaining accurate case documentation. I have learned how important it is to build trust with people, especially when they may feel overwhelmed or unsure about asking for help.

One of the things I enjoy most about my work is helping people feel heard and supported. I understand that reaching out for services can sometimes be intimidating, and I believe the way someone is treated during their first interaction can make a difference in whether they feel comfortable moving forward. I am patient, understanding, and comfortable having conversations with individuals from different backgrounds. I also have experience managing multiple responsibilities, meeting deadlines, and handling sensitive information professionally.

I am especially interested in Seven Starling because of the opportunity to help individuals connect with mental health services. My background in social work has taught me the importance of making care accessible and helping people overcome barriers that may prevent them from receiving the support they need. I would love the opportunity to use my experience and skills in a position where I can continue making a positive difference in people's lives.

Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience and dedication to helping others could benefit Seven Starling. I look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,  
Novalee Adams

candidates.cover_letter:
Good morning AWA and PRC hiring team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With over a decade of experience in healthcare documentation, quality assurance, training, and behavioral health intake coordination, I bring a strong combination of administrative expertise, compassionate client communication, and the ability to independently manage complex workflows in a remote environment.

In my current part-time role as an Intake Coordinator with Therapist of Color Collaborative, I serve as a primary point of contact for individuals seeking behavioral health services. My responsibilities include responding to client inquiries and referrals, verifying insurance eligibility, coordinating consultations and initial appointments, matching clients with appropriate providers, and maintaining consistent follow-up throughout the intake process. I also coordinate VA Community Care referrals and authorizations, helping clients navigate administrative requirements that might otherwise delay access to treatment.

Beyond my daily intake responsibilities, I have developed and standardized workflows, tracking systems, and reference materials to improve operational efficiency and continuity of care. I am also involved in training and supporting intake staff, ensuring that processes remain consistent and that clients receive accurate, timely information. These experiences have strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, maintain detailed documentation, and recognize opportunities to improve the admissions experience.

Previously, as a Scribe Trainer and Quality Assurance Manager with ScribeEMR, I supported a remote team of more than 30 medical scribes, conducted documentation audits, facilitated training, and collaborated with healthcare providers to maintain accuracy and compliance. This background has given me a strong foundation in electronic medical records, HIPAA-conscious documentation, and independent remote work.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the emphasis on being a compassionate and reliable first point of contact for individuals and families seeking treatment. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use services can be an overwhelming experience. I approach these interactions with patience, professionalism, and the understanding that clear communication and dependable follow-through can make a meaningful difference in someone's willingness and ability to access care.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience in behavioral health intake, insurance coordination, and workflow management to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background aligns with the needs of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Warm regards,

Tatyana Nembhard

questionnaire.response: Working on the hotlines has been an incredible masterclass in empathy, rapid critical thinking, and conflict resolution. I’ve realized that my favorite part of the job is the core human connection and the ability to guide people toward solutions. I'm looking to leave the crisis sector so I can bring those exact communication strengths into a new industry—one where I can focus on building positive client relationships and supporting a business's daily operations

questionnaire.text: Who was (or is) your direct supervisor in this role?
questionnaire.body: Please provide their name, title, professional email address, and phone number.

questionnaire.text: If we asked this supervisor about your performance, what would they say was your most significant area for growth, and why?
questionnaire.response: If you spoke to my supervisor, they would tell you that my biggest area for growth has been learning how to establish firm emotional boundaries and truly leave the work at the desk when my shift ends. Because the nature of a suicide prevention hotline involves helping individuals through their absolute darkest moments, my natural instinct early on was to carry that weight and constantly worry about the outcomes of my callers after logging off. My supervisor noticed this and coached me on the fact that absolute empathy without boundaries leads to rapid depletion, which ultimately impacts performance. Over the past year, I’ve worked hard to treat emotional boundaries as a professional skill. I developed rigorous post-shift decompression routines and learned to trust the crisis continuum of care once a caller was safely handed off. My supervisor would tell you that I’ve made massive strides here, and that this growth is exactly why I can bring a highly resilient, deeply focused, and level-headed energy to your team without risking the quality of my output

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I'm applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. I want to be upfront that I haven't worked in behavioral health admissions. What I have done is the work that comes right before care starts: answering the phone, figuring out what someone needs, checking their insurance, and getting them scheduled.

Most recently I was a Bilingual Patient Access Representative at CHN, working from home. I took about 50 calls a day, verified insurance, ran through screening questions, and booked appointments. I was often the only Spanish speaker a patient could reach, and many of them were nervous or confused about their coverage. Before that, at J.P. Farley, I reviewed insurance claims and checked member eligibility, and I used Zendesk to keep track of what people asked and what I told them.
At Madison Metropolitan School District I worked with families directly. I interviewed parents, helped connect them with food, housing, and other resources, and made sure they understood what came next. At my school job in Cleveland I interpreted for parents at IEP meetings, which are not easy conversations to sit through. I learned how to slow down, use plain words, and wait for the question a parent is afraid to ask.

My degree is in Human Services with a concentration in social work, and Spanish is my first language. I know a first call can be the hardest one a family makes. I keep things simple, I don't rush, and I follow up on what I said I would do.

I'm used to working from home without someone checking on me, and I'm comfortable keeping my own list of people to call back. I would welcome the chance to talk with you.
Thank you for your time.

Sincerely,

Glory Chevere Quinones

Dear Hiring Manager,
Hello! 
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. candidates.cover_letter:
I am writing to express my interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. Although I am only 23 years old, I have gained valuable hands-on experience working with individuals from challenging backgrounds through foster parenting, corrections, and my current role as a caseworker for the State of Utah. These experiences have helped shape my passion for helping others, particularly adolescents who are navigating difficult circumstances and working toward a healthier, more successful future.

For a year and a half, I served as a foster parent, which gave me firsthand experience understanding the patience, consistency, compassion, and dedication it takes to support youth who have experienced trauma and instability. This experience taught me the importance of creating a safe environment, building trust, advocating for individual needs, and recognizing that progress looks different for everyone.

I also spent one year working in corrections, where I developed valuable skills in communication, conflict resolution, maintaining professional boundaries, and working with individuals facing difficult life circumstances. This experience strengthened my ability to remain calm under pressure, approach challenging situations with understanding, and recognize the importance of accountability alongside compassion.

Currently, I work as a caseworker for the State of Utah, where I continue to develop my skills in advocacy, case management, problem-solving, and working with individuals and families who need support and guidance. My current position has further reinforced my belief that people deserve to be met with dignity, understanding, and opportunities to make meaningful changes in their lives.

I believe my combination of professional experience and personal experience gives me a unique perspective when working with adolescents. I understand that young people need more than someone telling them what they should do. They need positive role models, consistency, encouragement, accountability, and people who are willing to meet them where they are. I strive to be someone who can build meaningful connections while maintaining appropriate boundaries and helping individuals recognize their own potential.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my experience, work ethic, and passion for helping others to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am eager to continue growing professionally while making a meaningful difference in the lives of the adolescents and families your organization serves.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience could benefit your team.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Admissions and Intake position with Adolescent Wellness. With a background in healthcare administration, patient admissions, and remote patient advocacy, I bring valuable experience in patient coordination, compassionate communication, and navigating complex healthcare needs. More importantly, I have a genuine passion for mental health advocacy and a strong desire to dedicate my career to helping individuals who are struggling.

In my previous role as a Ward Secretary at Heritage Manor, I regularly assisted with patient admissions, intake paperwork, medical records, and communication between patients, families, and healthcare professionals. This experience provided me with a strong foundation in healthcare administration, confidentiality, and supporting patients during important transitions in their care.

Currently, as a Patient Advocate with Understood Care, I independently manage patient cases, verify insurance benefits, coordinate appointments, communicate with healthcare providers, and help individuals overcome barriers to receiving necessary services. Many of the patients I assist are experiencing difficult or overwhelming circumstances, and I take pride in being someone who listens, advocates for their needs, and follows through until they receive meaningful assistance.

What particularly draws me to Adolescent Wellness is the opportunity to work directly with individuals and families affected by mental health and substance use challenges. Mental health is a cause I care deeply about, and I strongly believe that everyone deserves to be treated with dignity, compassion, and understanding, regardless of their circumstances. I recognize how much courage it can take for someone to reach out for help, and I would find tremendous purpose in being one of the first people to offer reassurance, guidance, and a pathway toward treatment.

While my professional background spans different areas of healthcare, my long-term interest is in behavioral health. I am eager to expand my knowledge of mental health and substance use treatment admissions while contributing the practical skills I have already developed through years of patient-facing experience. I am comfortable handling sensitive conversations, maintaining confidential records, managing multiple responsibilities independently, and providing consistent follow-through.

I am not simply seeking another position in healthcare. I am looking for an opportunity to contribute to work that I genuinely believe in, where compassion and advocacy can make a meaningful difference in someone’s life. I would be proud to bring that dedication, along with my admissions experience and strong work ethic, to the team at Adolescent Wellness.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, commitment, and genuine passion for mental health advocacy could contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,
Brett Bankston

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Administrative Assistant III position. With approximately 10 years of professional experience in administrative support, customer service, healthcare operations, scheduling, and public service, I believe I have the skills, knowledge, and dedication necessary to make a positive contribution to your organization.

In January 2026, I graduated from Colorado State University Global with a bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice and Criminal Forensics. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my administrative experience, strong work ethic, adaptability, and commitment to excellent customer service to your team. Sincerely,

November 4, 2026

Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator Position

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. Throughout my career, I have found that the most meaningful work I do is helping individuals and families navigate difficult circumstances, access support, and feel heard during vulnerable moments. Your organization’s focus on supporting adolescents and their well-being strongly resonates with me, both professionally and personally.

I bring nearly a decade of experience in case management, behavioral health, youth services, and client advocacy. Through my work with the International Rescue Committee, Cayuga Centers, and The People Concern, I have supported adolescents and families facing complex emotional, social, and behavioral health challenges. My responsibilities have included conducting intake assessments and virtual interviews, coordinating referrals, maintaining confidential documentation, and guiding families through unfamiliar systems with patience and compassion.

These experiences have taught me that the first interaction someone has with an organization can make a meaningful difference. Whether speaking with a concerned parent, supporting a young person in crisis, or helping someone understand their available resources, I approach each conversation with empathy, professionalism, and a commitment to finding solutions.

As a bilingual English-Spanish professional, I also value the opportunity to connect with families from diverse backgrounds and help reduce barriers to accessing services.

What particularly draws me to this opportunity is the chance to combine my professional experience with work that I genuinely care about. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to a team dedicated to helping adolescents and families take meaningful steps toward healing and stability.

Thank you for considering my application. I would be grateful for the opportunity to discuss how my background and commitment to compassionate client care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Maria Rebecca Romero

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in Adolescent Mental Health and Substance Use Treatment. With nearly three years of experience working in a medical office, my Medical Assistant certification, and my current pursuit of a Bachelor's degree in Psychology, I am eager to bring my healthcare background, communication skills, and passion for helping others to your team.

Throughout my experience in the medical field, I have developed an understanding of the importance of patient-centered care, professionalism, confidentiality, and compassionate communication. Working in a healthcare environment has allowed me to build valuable skills in interacting with patients, handling sensitive information, and helping individuals navigate their healthcare needs. Although my professional background has not been specifically within mental health, my education and growing interest in psychology have strengthened my desire to pursue a career where I can make a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals facing mental health and substance use challenges.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because of the importance of providing adolescents and their families with support, guidance, and access to the care they need. I understand that reaching out for treatment can be an emotional and overwhelming experience, and I believe every individual deserves to be met with patience, compassion, understanding, and respect. I would welcome the opportunity to use my healthcare experience and interpersonal skills to help make the admissions process as supportive and comfortable as possible for patients and their families.

I am motivated to continue learning and growing professionally while contributing to a team that makes a positive impact on the lives of adolescents and their families. Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background, education, and enthusiasm for this field could make me a valuable addition to your team.

Sincerely,
Kimber Jureczki

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a recent Master of Social Work graduate with experience supporting adolescents and individuals navigating mental health challenges, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to an organization dedicated to improving the emotional well-being of young people and their families.
Through my internship at Partnership with Children, I gained valuable experience working with high school students experiencing emotional, behavioral, and social challenges. I provided individual support, assisted students with emotional regulation and anger management, participated in crisis interventions, and helped students navigate personal and academic barriers. This experience strengthened my ability to build rapport with adolescents, establish supportive relationships, and approach each individual's circumstances with empathy and understanding.

Additionally, my previous experience in an outpatient mental health setting allowed me to work with individuals experiencing serious mental health conditions, including schizophrenia. I developed skills in monitoring changes in behavior and mental status, recognizing signs of decompensation, supporting medication adherence, and identifying when additional clinical intervention was necessary. These experiences strengthened my ability to remain calm in challenging situations, recognize potential safety concerns, and communicate effectively with members of a multidisciplinary team.
I am particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy's commitment to creating a supportive environment where adolescents can work through mental health challenges while developing healthier coping strategies and building resilience. I believe in meeting youth where they are, recognizing their individual strengths, and understanding the environmental and family factors that influence their overall well-being.

As a developing social work professional, I would bring compassion, patience, strong communication skills, and a genuine commitment to serving vulnerable populations. I am eager to continue growing professionally while contributing my education, experience, and dedication to your team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience align with the needs of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Best regards, 
Denisse Lino

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I know how hard it can be to ask for help, especially when you’re already overwhelmed and don’t know where to start. Being the person who can make that conversation feel a little easier is work I care about. That’s what drew me to the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

At FLOOD Ministries, I was in charge of all client intake and maintained electronic client records. A big part of my job was helping people get comfortable during a very uncomfortable time. I listened, walked them through the process, and helped connect them with resources. I wanted people to feel like they could ask questions and be honest about what they needed without feeling judged.

At Behavior Frontiers, I gained experience with insurance verification and supporting children under clinical supervision. I also completed the 40-hour Registered Behavior Technician training. I’m currently working toward my bachelor’s degree in Behavioral Health Science with an emphasis in Substance Use Disorders at Grand Canyon University, and I completed UC San Diego’s 80-hour ASCEND SUD Counselor Core Competency Training. I’m excited to put what I’m learning into work that helps people access care.

This work matters to me outside of school and employment, too. I’m a mom, an older sibling, and heavily involved in our local high school football team’s mental health activities. While I haven’t held a formal remote position, I know how to keep myself on task and get things done. Between online classes, running a business, and managing social media for local companies, I’m used to taking responsibility for my workload. I’m very trainable and open to feedback. Give me clear expectations, teach me your process, and I’ll put in the effort to learn it well. If I don’t know something, I’ll ask.

I also bring years of customer service, sales, and management experience. I’m comfortable talking with people, following up, keeping records organized, and staying calm when a conversation gets difficult. I would love the opportunity to bring that experience and my personality to your team, helping callers feel welcome while making sure the details get handled.

Thank you for considering me. I’d appreciate the chance to talk about what I can bring to your admissions team and learn more about what you need.

Sincerely,

To the Hiring Manager,
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With nearly four years of experience in remote healthcare admissions and administrative coordination at DaVita, I have developed a strong background in referral processing, medical record review, insurance verification, and coordinating with healthcare professionals to help patients access appropriate care. I would love the opportunity to bring this experience to an organization focused on supporting adolescents and families navigating mental health and substance use treatment.
In my previous role at DaVita, I was responsible for reviewing and processing incoming hospital referrals, gathering and auditing medical documentation, coordinating outstanding records and lab results, and communicating with hospital case managers, social workers, and other healthcare professionals. I understand how important timely communication, thorough documentation, and compassionate coordination are when someone is seeking treatment. I would bring a patient-centered approach to helping prospective clients and their families navigate the admissions process and connect with the appropriate resources.
I am also currently pursuing an education in social work, which has further strengthened my interest in behavioral health, patient advocacy, and helping individuals access supportive and appropriate services. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to contribute to a treatment environment that supports adolescents and their families during what can be a difficult and vulnerable time.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my healthcare admissions experience, administrative skills, and commitment to patient-centered care could contribute to the Adolescent Wellness Academy team.

Mia Cedeno

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With several years of experience in healthcare administration and patient services, along with a background in psychology and behavioral science, I believe I would bring a strong combination of patient-centered communication, organization, and compassion to your team.

During my time at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center, I worked directly with patients to help them navigate the healthcare process. My responsibilities included scheduling appointments, assisting with patient intake, verifying insurance eligibility, coordinating referrals and authorizations, resolving administrative issues, and communicating with patients, providers, and insurance representatives. I learned how important it is to make people feel heard, provide clear information, and help them understand what steps to take next. I also gained experience working remotely, managing competing priorities independently, and maintaining accurate documentation while handling sensitive patient information.

What interests me most about this opportunity is the chance to use my healthcare experience in a setting where the work can make such a meaningful difference in someone's life. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be a difficult and sometimes overwhelming experience for individuals and their families. I would approach those conversations with patience, empathy, professionalism, and the understanding that the first interaction can have a lasting impact on someone's willingness to seek care.

My educational background in behavioral science, along with my ongoing studies toward a bachelor's degree in psychology, has strengthened my interest in mental health and human behavior. I am especially interested in continuing to grow within this field while bringing the practical healthcare experience I have already developed. I am comfortable learning new systems and processes, communicating across multiple platforms, and balancing attention to detail with the human side of patient care.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, work ethic, and genuine interest in helping others to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.

Sincerely,
Cheyenne Rogers

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a professional background in education, supporting individuals with diverse needs, and communicating with families during challenging situations, I believe I can bring compassion, professionalism, and strong organizational skills to your admissions team.

Through my experience as a second-grade teacher and working with children with developmental and learning disabilities, I have developed the ability to communicate effectively, remain calm under pressure, and approach sensitive situations with patience and understanding. I recognize the importance of making individuals and families feel heard, respected, and supported, especially when they are navigating difficult circumstances.

My professional experience has required me to manage multiple responsibilities, maintain accurate documentation, communicate consistently with families, and provide individualized support based on each person’s needs. I am comfortable handling confidential information, learning new systems, and working independently while maintaining a high level of accountability.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to make a meaningful difference through the very first interaction someone has with your organization. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming step, and I would be honored to help individuals and families feel comfortable, informed, and confident as they explore their options.

Although my background is primarily in education and individualized support rather than behavioral health admissions, I am eager to apply my transferable skills, expand my knowledge, and contribute to a team dedicated to helping people access the care they need.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, communication skills, and dedication to helping others could benefit your organization.

Sincerely,

Attisa Adiki

candidates.cover_letter:
Allison Bertolino
Port Saint Lucie, FL 34983

October 20, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescence Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining Adolescence Wellness Academy. With over three years of experience in behavioral health admissions, client assessments, insurance verification, treatment coordination, and patient intake, I have developed a strong understanding of the importance of compassionate, efficient, and individualized care. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, professionalism, and dedication to your team and contribute to helping adolescents and their families access the support and treatment they need.

In my current role as Lead Day Time Admissions Coordinator at Archstone Behavioral Health, I oversee the admissions process from the initial inquiry through enrollment. My responsibilities include verifying insurance benefits, conducting comprehensive assessments and screenings, identifying potential substance use disorders, and helping determine appropriate levels of care. I also coordinate travel arrangements, maintain accurate and confidential client records, and collaborate with probation officers and court officials when coordinating mandated treatment services. These responsibilities have strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, communicate effectively with individuals and families during difficult circumstances, and ensure a smooth and supportive admissions experience.

My previous experience as an Admissions Coordinator with Magnolia Ranch Recovery and Genesis Detox further developed my skills in client communication, treatment coordination, documentation, and collaboration with multidisciplinary teams to support individualized treatment planning. In addition, my experience as a Customer Service Manager strengthened my leadership, problem-solving, organization, and conflict-resolution skills. I understand the importance of building trust, responding to concerns with empathy, maintaining confidentiality, and helping people navigate what can often be an overwhelming process.

I believe my combination of behavioral health admissions experience, strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and compassionate approach would make me a valuable addition to Adolescence Wellness Academy. I am especially interested in the opportunity to apply my experience in a setting focused on supporting adolescents and their families, where clear communication, patience, and a commitment to quality care are essential.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and dedication to behavioral health can contribute to the mission of Adolescence Wellness Academy. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.

Sincerely,
Allison Bertolino

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Clinical Intake Specialist position. With a Master of Social Work degree and experience providing clinical services across outpatient, emergency department, and school-based settings, I bring a strong foundation in clinical assessment, risk evaluation, crisis intervention, and care coordination.

Throughout my clinical experience, I have conducted psychosocial and mental health assessments, evaluated suicide and self-harm risk, developed individualized safety plans, and identified appropriate treatment recommendations and referrals. My experience in the emergency department strengthened my ability to assess presenting concerns, recognize immediate safety needs, and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to facilitate appropriate dispositions and continuity of care. In outpatient and school-based settings, I have further developed my ability to identify clinical needs, understand complex psychosocial factors, and support individuals and families in accessing appropriate services.

I am particularly interested in this position because it aligns with my strengths in clinical assessment, gathering relevant psychosocial information, determining service needs, and helping individuals navigate the treatment process. I understand the importance of conducting thorough, compassionate, and clinically informed intakes while ensuring that safety concerns are appropriately addressed and clients are connected with suitable levels of care.

In addition to my assessment and crisis intervention experience, I bring strong communication, documentation, and interdisciplinary collaboration skills. I am comfortable working with diverse populations, including children, adolescents, adults, and families, and approach each interaction with professionalism, empathy, and sound clinical judgment.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, assessment skills, and commitment to quality mental health care would contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Shannon Beaton

candidates.cover_letter:
To whom it may concern,
My name is Selena, and I am excited to be applying for the primary therapist position at North Carolina's first-ever AWA location! I am an LCSWA with multiple years of experience providing therapeutic support in numerous capacities, including as a behavioral health technician, case manager, and psychotherapist. I've also gained experience in a diverse range of therapeutic settings, such as an inpatient adolescent hospital, PHP/IOP mental health clinics, community health (including in-home), and outpatient therapy. The most influential experiences I've gained have been working in adolescent inpatient and PHP/IOP clinics, in which I became comfortable leading group therapy sessions, providing 1:1 individual therapy as well as family-based therapy, and working collaboratively with clinical teams consisting of numerous disciplines and treatment goals. I've also become comfortable with higher levels of care, which I am able to use to offer clients validation and unconditional positive regard, as these experiences can be exhausting. In my current outpatient work, I primarily work with pre-teens and adolescents, as I witnessed a gap in care for these age groups despite the intensity of these transformative years. I aspire to be a supportive resource to these clients in whatever capacity I am able to, as it is already difficult to be a teen, let alone one who feels misunderstood and alone in the journey.

candidates.cover_letter:
I am pleased to apply for this position. I hold a Master’s degree in Human Services Counseling and I bring extensive experience in behavioral health, crisis intervention, child welfare, and program coordination. Throughout my career, I have valued the opportunity to help individuals and families navigate difficult circumstances and connect with meaningful support.
Most recently, I served as an Anti-Human Trafficking and Child Exploitation Coordinator with the National Youth Advocate Program. My work included coordinating services and referrals, collaborating with community partners and multidisciplinary teams, reviewing records for quality and compliance, and providing training and technical assistance. This experience strengthened my ability to manage sensitive situations, communicate clearly, and follow through on complex needs.
My background also includes group counseling and psychoeducation, trauma-informed care, clinical documentation, and supporting children, adolescents, and families. I am comfortable working independently in a remote environment, navigating multiple computer systems, and balancing responsibilities while maintaining attention to detail. I speak English, Portuguese, and Spanish, which helps me connect with people from diverse backgrounds.
I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, compassion, and strong sense of responsibility to your team. I approach my work with patience, professionalism, and a willingness to learn, and I take pride in helping people feel heard and respected.
Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to this position.

Sincerely,
Vivian Oliveira
